page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.n1.medium is an entry-level virtual machine instance belonging to the ecs.n1 server family. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz. The instance is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It operates on the KVM hypervisor and uses the x86_64 architecture. No local storage or GPU accelerators are bundled with this instance type, and it includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results indicate that the ecs.n1.medium delivers entry-level performance. In CPU-focused tests, the instance achieved a stress-ng single-core score of 1108.59 and a multi-core score of 2194.17. Memory performance is similarly constrained, with a read-only large block bandwidth of 16.3 GB/sec and a write large block bandwidth of 14.46 GB/sec. Cryptographic and compression tasks also reflect these limitations, with a single-threaded gzip compression speed of 19.19 GB/sec and a Passmark CPU encryption score of 825.7.

Given the dedicated CPU allocation but low overall resource density, this instance offers a predictable but limited compute profile. It is suitable for lightweight, non-resource-intensive workloads such as basic static web serving, which benchmarked at 1.9 GB/sec, or low-traffic Redis caching, where it handled 2.87 million SET operations per second. It is not suited for memory-intensive databases, software compilation, or parallel processing tasks, as evidenced by its low Passmark database operations score of 570.41 and Geekbench multi-core score of 1698.0.

Operating under the KVM hypervisor, its performance profile is modest, as demonstrated by a stress-ng single-core score of 1108.59 and a multi-core score of 2194.17. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with large block write speeds of 14.46 GB/sec. Given these hardware constraints and lower-tier benchmark results, such as a static web serving throughput of 1.9 GB/sec and a Passmark database score of 570.41, the ecs.n1.medium is best suited for lightweight, predictable workloads like basic web serving, simple application testing, or low-volume Redis caching.
